html:
Tripolitania is the north-western region of Libya around the city of Tripoli. On the map, from 1715 to 1815, it is the Ottoman province of Tripoli under the Karamanli dynasty, which ruled it almost as an independent state from 1711 to 1835.

The region had been part of Carthage, then Rome, then the Muslim world. The Ottomans took Tripoli in 1551. In 1711 Ahmed Karamanli, an officer of Turkish descent, seized power and made the governorship hereditary. His family ruled Tripoli and, through a governor in Benghazi, Cyrenaica.

Tripoli lived from caravans crossing the Sahara through the Fezzan, part of the trans-Saharan trade, and from corsairs. Yusuf Karamanli's demand for more tribute from the United States led to the First Barbary War of 1801 to 1805. Debt and civil war followed, and in 1835 the Ottomans restored direct rule. Italy took the region in 1911; see Libya.
